terms.definition: An economy in which materials are kept in use by reuse, repair and recycling, so that waste and the use of new resources are minimised.
terms.examiner: Contrast with the linear "take, make, dispose" economy.

terms.definition: An economy in which resources are extracted, made into products and thrown away after use.
terms.examiner: Leads to resource depletion and waste.

terms.definition: The area of land and water needed to supply the resources a population uses and to absorb its wastes.
The ability of an area to produce renewable resources and absorb wastes.
terms.examiner: When the footprint is greater than biocapacity there is ecological overshoot.

terms.definition: Designing products so that at the end of their life the materials become the raw materials for new products.
terms.examiner: Design for disassembly makes the materials easy to separate.

terms.definition: Designs that copy structures or processes found in living organisms.
The total greenhouse gas emissions caused by an activity, product or person, expressed as carbon dioxide equivalent.
terms.examiner: Includes indirect emissions from making and transporting goods.
